faq.a: The Ganges, called the Padma there, the Brahmaputra, called the Jamuna, and the Meghna all join in Bangladesh. Together with hundreds of smaller rivers, they make one of the biggest river systems on Earth.
Most of Bangladesh is less than 10 metres above sea level, because it sits on the huge Ganges–Brahmaputra delta. Only the hills in the north-east and south-east are much higher.

faq.q: Why does the monsoon cause floods?
faq.a: Most of the year’s rain falls in the four monsoon months, June to September. The ground fills up with water and the rivers, already swollen by Himalayan meltwater, overflow their banks.
asks: When is flood season in Bangladesh?

faq.q: How does Bangladesh protect people from cyclones?
faq.a: Bangladesh has early warnings, tens of thousands of trained volunteers who spread the alert, and thousands of raised cyclone shelters. Mangrove forests on the coast also help soften storm waves.

faq.q: Are floods always bad in Bangladesh?
faq.a: No. Ordinary yearly floods, called barsha, bring fertile mud and water for rice and fish. Only extreme floods, called bonna, destroy homes and crops.
asks: Do floods help farmers in Bangladesh?

facts: In an average year about a fifth of Bangladesh is flooded during the monsoon.
The Bhola cyclone of 1970 killed an estimated 300,000 to 500,000 people in what is now Bangladesh.
Bangladesh's Cyclone Preparedness Programme, started in 1972, trains tens of thousands of volunteers.
